answer.summary: Bangaly Kaba recommends using the “managing complex change” framework: assess five ingredients, use the team’s symptoms to locate gaps, then choose the levers that address what is missing.

sections.heading: Framework and diagnosis
sections.content: The five components are vision, skills, incentives, resources, and an action plan. As a leader, observe what is happening and identify challenges both anecdotally and from what you see. The framework links missing components to symptoms: missing vision can produce confusion; missing incentives, resistance; missing an action plan, false starts; and missing skills, anxiety. Use those signals to decide which component or “bucket” needs attention.

sections.heading: Address the gap
sections.content: After identifying the likely bucket, work out what is missing and which levers to pull; focus your effort there to improve the team. Kaba notes that action plans can be easier to institute than components further to the left in the framework, so diagnosing the specific gap helps direct attention rather than applying a generic fix.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately describes the five-part “managing complex change” framework, using observed symptoms to locate missing components and identify the appropriate levers. It also notes that action plans are generally easier to institute than components farther left in the framework, which captures Kaba’s contrast with harder-to-change areas such as vision and skills.
